llm.summary: This skill appears to handle credentials and send project data to an external service, but its Maven purpose is mixed with unrelated Gaokao/XBY configuration, so it needs careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: The stated Maven dependency-management purpose does not cleanly match the reported implementation: configuration references Gaokao/XBY API-key handling while tool wrappers send Maven/project metadata to a remote API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill asks for an API key, stores it locally, forwards workspace/POM/dependency data externally, and may show raw API responses without enough documented scoping or minimization.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No malicious installer behavior was shown, and VirusTotal telemetry was clean; the main issue is runtime credential/data handling rather than package installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access and project metadata transfer can be proportionate for remote dependency analysis, but the unrelated service naming and under-disclosed data flow make the requested environment access overbroad for the advertised purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The reported code persists an API key into a local .env file, which is sensitive persistence and appears insufficiently consented or bounded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and remote XBY/XiaoBenYang-style backend. Use a revocable API key, avoid scanning private repositories until the publisher clarifies exactly what project data is uploaded, and remove any stored .env key when you stop using the skill.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a transparency concern: environment, file, and network use may fit a remote analysis skill, but the disclosures do not appear to cover credential persistence and external data transfer clearly enough.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: unrelated Gaokao/XBY naming and credential flow conflict with the Maven-facing purpose.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: leftover Gaokao-style project references materially weaken artifact coherence.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: XBY_APIKEY handling in a Maven skill is not purpose-aligned unless clearly documented, which the supplied evidence does not show.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the config docstring naming a different Gaokao skill supports the mismatch concern.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: asking for and saving an API key to .env needs explicit consent, storage location disclosure, and removal guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: returning API results is expected, but raw unsanitized output can expose more data than necessary.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: writing the API key locally without clear confirmation is sensitive persistence.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: sending POM/dependency data to an API can fit remote dependency analysis, but paths, scan results, and project configuration need clearer consent and minimization.
